The customer is the value-for-money buyer.
They like: budget-friendly price; mid-range price; feature-rich, does a lot.
They dislike: premium price; made from sustainable / eco materials; a trending, much-talked-about item.
These lists describe the customer's TASTE in general. Use ONLY facts that actually appear on this product's sheet: praise the sheet facts the customer likes, and do not bring up the ones they dislike AT ALL. Two things count as false and are scored against you: stating the opposite of a sheet fact, and claiming anything the sheet does not state at all. A liked trait that is not on this sheet is not available to you. If few likable facts apply, a shorter pitch is better than touching a disliked topic.

The customer is the identity-expressive buyer.
They like: has only a small number of owners; premium price; made from sustainable / eco materials; provides only the essential functions, with few extras.
They dislike: already has a large user base; budget-friendly price (do NOT bring this up); a trending, much-talked-about item.
